title: Linux Kernel 1.0.0 Release
summary: The official 1.0 release of the free open-source monolithic Unix-like operating system kernel created by Finnish student Linus Torvalds.
facts: Linus Torvalds announced the original Linux project on Usenet comp.os.minix in August 1991.
Version 1.0.0 was released on March 14, 1994 with 176,250 lines of code.
Dual-licensed under the GNU General Public License (GPLv2).

title: Slackware Linux Distribution
summary: The oldest surviving Linux distribution, created by Patrick Volkerding to provide an authentic Unix-like computing environment installed via floppy disks.
facts: Originally based on the SLS (Softlanding Linux System) distribution.
Distributed as sets of 3.5-inch floppy disk images named A, N, X, and Y.
Emphasized simplicity, stability, and minimal distribution modification.

title: Debian GNU/Linux
summary: Community-driven non-commercial Linux distribution founded by Ian Murdock, renowned for the dpkg package system, APT, and the Debian Social Contract.
facts: Named 'Debian' as a portmanteau of Murdock's girlfriend Debra Lynn and his first name Ian.
Sponsored early on by Richard Stallman's Free Software Foundation (FSF).
Pioneered automated dependency resolution package management with Advanced Packaging Tool (APT).

title: Red Hat Linux 1.0
summary: Pioneering commercial Linux distribution that popularized the RPM Package Manager and brought open-source enterprise OS support to corporate IT.
facts: Founded by Marc Ewing, who wore a red Cornell lacrosse hat given by his grandfather.
Introduced RPM (Red Hat Package Manager) package file format.
Became the first major open-source company to go public in August 1999.

title: Tux the Linux Penguin
summary: The world-famous official mascot of the Linux kernel, created by Larry Ewing using GIMP software following Linus Torvalds' love for penguins.
facts: Created during a logo competition held on Linux kernel mailing lists in 1996.
Drawn using early versions of GIMP (GNU Image Manipulation Program).
Name stands for '(T)orvalds (U)ni(X)' as well as referring to a tuxedo appearance.
